summary.headline: Spandana Q1 FY27 PAT rose to INR12 crore from INR5 crore in Q4, with AUM at INR4,887 crore (+11% QoQ) and marginal cost of borrowing at 11.3%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 showed improvement across growth, asset quality, funding cost and profitability. AUM grew 11% QoQ to INR4,887 crore, and new-book (post-April 2025 sourcing) share rose to 91%. Annualised credit cost fell to 2.1% from 3.2%, with net credit cost negative on recoveries, and NIM widened to 12.5% from 9.9%. Management reiterated FY27 gross credit cost of 2.5-3%, net credit cost near 2%, and an AUM exit of a little over INR6,000 crore for FY27.

segments.name: Microfinance lending (core)
segments.commentary: AUM INR4,887 crore; top 5-6 states (MP, Bihar, Andhra, Telangana, Odisha, West Bengal) about 60-65% of book. Tamil Nadu share about INR16 crore and Maharashtra about INR288 crore, against industry of INR38,000 crore and INR24,000 crore respectively.

segments.name: Individual loan product (pilot)
segments.commentary: Ready for pilot in 8 MP branches with 8-10 staff over next 3 months, initially for existing customers with eNACH; intended to later extend to new customers and to group company Criss Financial.

guidance_outlook: FY27 gross credit cost maintained at 2.5-3%; Q1 was 2.1% and efforts are to retain it.
FY27 net credit cost closer to 2%, with recoveries from 90-plus pool of INR150-200 crore (aim slightly above INR200 crore; current run-rate INR16-18 crore a month).
FY27 business disbursement target INR6,000-6,500 crore; AUM exit FY27 a little above INR6,000 crore; March 2028 AUM about INR10,000 crore (to be firmed up around August-September).
FY27 opex about INR675 crore vs about INR760 crore in FY26; FY28 opex to rise about 10%.
ROA currently about 1%, expected to improve in FY27; 3.5% ROA viewed as feasible for FY28 on business-as-usual basis.
Marginal cost of borrowing expected to decline further as more CGS and PSU bank lines come in; no further lending-rate increases planned (last hike 1 October 2025).
INR200 crore rights issue balance (INR100 crore from promoter, INR100 crore from others) expected before end of Q2 FY27.
Branch count to stay about 1,250 standalone; some branch additions in Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu this year.
capex_capacity: About 1,250 standalone branches; no plan for further branch consolidation; 100 underperforming branches carved out for revival by a dedicated task force.
New LOS platform expected in UAT by end of Q2 FY27; migration from Jayam to Perfios platform planned for October-December 2026 across 1,250 branches.
Investments planned in Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra expansion and automation to reduce manual intake; savings to be reinvested.
Liquidity at INR1,316 crore; management says it may optimise liquidity over time but prefers to stay liquid.
demand_pricing: Disbursement and sourcing: new members 1.38 lakh, with 61% new-member share; new book at 91% of AUM under new credit guidelines, targeted to reach about 95% next quarter.
Yield at 24.6% vs ideal disbursement yield of about 25.25%; management expects marginal further improvement, then stabilisation.
Collections: X-bucket 99.5%; July collections in line with prior month, no adverse trend yet despite weak monsoon/El Nino risk; districts likely to be impacted have sourcing controls.
Credit guarantee scheme (CGS) sanctions of about INR545 crore, of which INR200 crore drawn (INR500 crore sanctioned at one point in Q&A) at about 10% or slightly above.
Competition and funding: more banks, including PSU banks, in talks; bank share of borrowings rose to 47%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 credit cost target of 2.5-3% still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes; Q1 annualised credit cost was 2.1% and the aim is to retain it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROA target for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Current ROA about 1%; FY27 expected to improve, with 3.5% considered feasible in FY28 on a business-as-usual basis.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net credit cost outlook for FY27 including recoveries?
qa_highlights.answer: Closer to 2% net; recoveries from the 90-plus pool expected at INR150-200 crore, with the older pool stopping collections from next year.

qa_highlights.question: How much recovery is expected from the written-off/90-plus pool against cumulative slippages?
qa_highlights.answer: The 90-plus pool is about INR2,500 crore; about INR326 crore collected over the last 18 months; current run-rate INR16-18 crore a month.

qa_highlights.question: Will the yield keep rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Ideal disbursement yield about 25.25% and current yield close to it, so marginal improvement expected before stabilising; last rate increase was October 2025 and no further hikes planned.

qa_highlights.question: Are there any signs of stress from the weak monsoon?
qa_highlights.answer: No adverse observation in collection efficiency so far in July; proactive sourcing controls in affected districts.

qa_highlights.question: Stage 1 provisioning looks low at about 40 bps versus peers at 1%+; will it be raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed it is a valid point and is working on it; target to raise the 1-30 bucket collections bar to 50%.

risks_watch: El Nino and weak monsoon: management says no adverse collection signs in July so far, but districts likely to be impacted are under proactive sourcing controls; watch X-bucket efficiency (99.5%) and 1-90 bucket (1.2% of AUM) next quarter.

Recovery dependence: FY27 net credit cost near 2% relies on INR150-200 crore recoveries from the 90-plus pool (about INR2,500 crore, INR326 crore collected over 18 months); current run-rate INR16-18 crore a month, and the older pool stops being collected from next year.
Stage 1 provisioning at about 40 bps, which an analyst contrasted with peers at 1% or more; management is working on it and targets raising the 1-30 bucket collections bar to 50%.

Funding: only about INR200 crore of INR1,597 crore borrowed in Q1 was under CGS (INR545 crore sanctioned, INR200 crore drawn); bank share 47%; further PSU bank lines and marginal cost decline are expected but not yet committed.

Execution: new LOS platform UAT by end Q2 FY27 and migration from Jayam to Perfios across about 1,250 branches in October-December 2026; INR200 crore rights issue balance expected before end Q2 FY27; FY28 AUM about INR10,000 crore to be firmed up in August-September.
Liquidity at INR1,316 crore is above business-as-usual; management may optimise it over time but prefers to remain liquid, so deployment pace and margin impact are open questions.
key_quotes: Annualized credit cost at 2.1% (Net credit cost remained negative in Q1, due to stronger recoveries during the period) against 3.2% in the March quarter.
So overall business is looking good, but that should not lead to complacency.
So it's a wait and watch with adequate controls.
There can be some blips here and there depending upon the situation, but large things will not happen if you have your process and controls in place.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on Q1 execution (collections, pricing, funding), but deliberately cautious on the macro, saying El Nino is a "wait and watch" and warning against complacency. Management is firm on not raising lending rates and on the 2.5-3% gross credit cost target, while leaving FY28 AUM and ROA as directional rather than firm guidance.
